reason: #4831, not mechanical: an async network fetch of external authority records, then an upsert of the AuthoritySnapshot cache; an action would run the fetch inside the write transaction or carry the fetched records as audit params. Needs a decision: audit the cache write, or classify it as a cache (by-design).

#4831, not mechanical: ruled 2026-10-04 to retire in favour of the registry's undo; it now serves only MutationLog rows with no undoable action behind them (#4864). Wrapping an undo route in its own action would add a third trail; it goes when those rows have actions.

read-only: scores candidate links from existing rows and returns them, no db.save/delete/transaction anywhere in the body — POST is used because the request body carries top_k and entity_id, not because it mutates. Reclassified 2026-09-18 after reading the whole function.

#4831, not mechanical: loads a PyKEEN model and scores every claim before writing links; inside registry.invoke that work would hold the library write transaction. Needs a job-shaped action (a ruling on long-running actions).
#4831, not mechanical: synchronous PyKEEN training (30 s to minutes); inside registry.invoke it would hold the library write transaction. Needs a job-shaped action.

#4831, not mechanical: deletes a model from the PyKEEN inference store on disk; the route has no library database, and adding one changes its OpenAPI operation. Needs a decision on where model-store actions are audited.
#4831, not mechanical: writes a StoredPrediction to the PyKEEN inference store, not the library; the route has no library database for the audit row. Same decision as delete_trained_model.

#4831, not mechanical: rebuilds the derived stores (LanceDB vectors, kg.nt) from canonical rows, synchronously and at length; inside registry.invoke it would hold the write transaction. Canonical rows are not changed. Needs a job-shaped action or a by-design ruling for derived-store rebuilds.

read-only: composes existing KnowledgeClaim rows into prose via db.get() only, no db.save/delete anywhere in the body — POST is used because the request body carries a list of claim_ids, not because it mutates.

read-only by construction: rejects any mutating SPARQL verb (INSERT/DELETE/DROP/CLEAR/LOAD/CREATE/COPY/MOVE/ADD) before running the query, per its own docstring ("Read-only; mutating verbs are rejected").
same read-only-by-construction guard as sparql_query (legacy path alias).

read-only: fetches candidate Wikidata statements via SPARQL and returns them for the user to review before import — no db.save/delete anywhere in the body. The mutating sibling, enrich_import, now calls registry.invoke() (entity.enrich_import, #4831 batch 4) and is no longer allowlisted here.
